intended_object: The canonical isomorphism of topological additive structures ∏_i F_i ≅ (∏_{i : P i} F_i) × (∏_{i : ¬P i} F_i). It splits a product into the factors whose index satisfies P and those whose index does not. This is read off the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The underlying bijection is Mathlib's `Equiv.piEquivPiSubtypeProd`, which sends f to the pair (f restricted to {i | P i}, f restricted to {i | ¬P i}). Addition is pointwise on both sides, so `map_add'` holds by `rfl`. The map and its inverse are continuous because they come from Mathlib's `Homeomorph.piEquivPiSubtypeProd`. So the definition gives exactly the canonical splitting isomorphism.

It is stated at maximal generality. The index type is arbitrary, and each factor only needs `Add` and a topology. `classical` supplies decidability of P, so P can be any predicate.

I searched Mathlib for `piEquivPiSubtypeProd`. It has this splitting as a plain equivalence (`Equiv`), a homeomorphism (`Homeomorph`), a ring isomorphism (`RingEquiv`) and a measurable equivalence (`MeasurableEquiv`). It has no version as a continuous additive equivalence (`ContinuousAddEquiv`), so this definition fills a real gap.

The only possible remark is that there is no multiplicative version generated via `to_additive`. That does not make the additive one wrong or meaningfully too narrow.
